column1: # M1 query mix. Columns: id <TAB> kind <TAB> field <TAB> args...
# Vocabulary is Zipf-ranked: t0 is the most frequent term, rank grows with the
# base-36 suffix, so t0/t1 are high-frequency, tz mid, t2s and beyond low.
# Both runners read this file; ids join the two result sets.
# Query kinds the original M1 mix never covered. Added in M1.6 when sweeping
# them for the first time turned up the worst divergences in the project:
# prefix/wildcard were 43x-560x slower than Lucene, because the wildcard family
# unioned its terms' postings by concatenating and sorting.
# Regexp shapes beyond q26's literal prefix, added when regexp became its own
# workstream: a leading wildcard, a broad class, alternation, a prefix with a
# wildcard middle, no literal prefix at all, and "contains". Each stresses a
# different part of the term-dictionary intersection.
# "Contains" and suffix shapes with a selective literal: what a term-level
# n-gram index answers without walking the dictionary.
# Mixed booleans in GenMixedBooleanScoring's S-expression grammar (the `sexpr`
# kind; the field column qualifies every term). These are the shapes the M2
# REST benchmark measured at 0.13-0.28x and routed to Lucene (`slower_shape`),
# because the port had no scorer tree: must+should, must_not, msm, boosts,
# constant_score, nesting. Both runners collect the top 50 with Lucene's
# Phrases inside the tree (read path R3): `exec::phrase::PhraseScorer`, two-phase.
